title: SJPD Flock ALPR misuse matter (disclosed Sept. 11, 2026): investigation, audit-trail, and access-suspension records

communications.subject: California Public Records Act Request: SJPD Flock ALPR misuse matter (disclosed Sept. 11, 2026): investigation, audit-trail, and access-suspension records
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the California Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

On September 11, 2026, Chief Paul Joseph disclosed that the Department terminated an officer who, while off duty, used a personal device to conduct unauthorized searches of the Department's Flock Safety automated license plate reader (ALPR) system in connection with a domestic violence matter involving family members. As reported, the Department has said that the improper access was discovered in February 2025, that the officer was placed on administrative leave and later terminated, that the matter was referred to the Commission on Peace Officer Standards and Training, that a criminal case was submitted to the District Attorney's office and no criminal charges were filed, and that audit logs tracking access from the personal device provided the evidence. Below, "the Flock misuse matter" refers to that matter.

Records requested:

1. Records of the Department's investigation of the Flock misuse matter and of the discipline imposed, to the extent they are records described in Penal Code § 832.7(b)(1), including any record relating to a sustained finding described in subparagraph (C) or (E) of that paragraph, and including the categories of records listed in Penal Code § 832.7(b)(3).

2. The ALPR access records the Department identified or relied on in the Flock misuse matter as reflecting the unauthorized searches: the corresponding entries of the Department's Flock organization audit, in native export form with every field the export carries (including date and time, search type, networks searched, time frame, reason, and case number), and any Flock record of the device, application, or access method used for those searches (for example, mobile application or web browser). License plate numbers and other civilian identifying information may be redacted. Civil Code § 1798.90.52 provides that an ALPR operator that accesses ALPR information "shall do both of the following: (a) Maintain a record of that access. At a minimum, the record shall include all of the following: (1) The date and time the information is accessed. (2) The license plate number or other data elements used to query the ALPR system. (3) The username of the person who accesses the information . . . . (4) The purpose for accessing the information." Duty Manual section L 4207 (2024) provides that "[a]udit trails shall be maintained by the Department for a minimum of two (2) years." A response of "no responsive records" to this item would mean that the Department no longer has the access records that, as reported, provided the evidence in the matter.

3. Records reflecting the suspension or disabling of the officer's access to the Flock ALPR system in the Flock misuse matter, including any request or authorization to disable the account and the Flock user-management record of the change.

If any record or portion of a record is withheld, please identify the exemption asserted for it and release any reasonably segregable portion. Please produce records for each item as they become available. I request electronic copies, with any audit-log export in its native spreadsheet or CSV format.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 calendar days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Brian Cervenka

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

1. Any main files, see-references, cross-references, and index entries on Anthony Neil Maffatone (born 1943, died Aug. 2, 2000), also known as “Tony Maffatone” and “Little Tony.” Please search all name variants, including “Anthony Nick Maffatone,” “Maffetone,” and the FBI’s own misspellings “Moffatone” and “Muffato.” Search the Central Records System, Sentinel, the Automated Case Support system, the Electronic Surveillance (ELSUR) indices, and field office indices, including Los Angeles, New York, and Newark.
2. All records in FBI file LA 122A-426, and in any corresponding FBI Headquarters or other field office files, that mention or refer to Anthony Maffatone. This includes the FD-302 of his interview on Nov. 16, 1988, in Los Angeles, which was indexed under “Anthony Neil Moffatone” and transcribed Nov. 29, 1988. It also includes any related FD-302s, 1A envelopes, interview notes, airtels, teletypes, memoranda, and grand jury–related correspondence.
3. All records reflecting communications between the FBI and Anthony Maffatone or his attorney concerning Martin Bacow, Sylvester Stallone, the film productions “Rhinestone,” “Rocky II,” “Cobra,” “Over the Top,” or “Rambo III,” or Maffatone’s stated willingness to testify before a federal grand jury.

Proof of death: Mr. Maffatone died on Aug. 2, 2000, in Suffolk County, New York. Proof of death can be found at the following link: https://www.findagrave.com/memorial/31264411/anthony-maffatone

Because the subject is deceased, his privacy interest is greatly diminished, and Exemptions 6 and 7(C) should not be used to withhold records about him.

For reference, a redacted version of the Nov. 16, 1988, FD-302 was released to me under FOI/PA# 1754808-000. That release withheld 10 pages as “duplicates.” Please process and release those pages in full where they fall within the scope of this request.

If any part of these documents are exempt from disclosure, please be sure to review and release all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions of responsive documents, as the FOIA requires.

I request that I be properly classified as a media requester. I am an assistant editor at Reason Magazine who has written numerous articles on topics of public interest, and I am requesting these documents in an editorial capacity. Please contact me if you have any questions about my media status.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Sincerely,

Matthew Petti

title: Private ALPRs

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Alabama Open Records Law, I hereby request the following records:

Good day,

I hope this finds you well.

I’m seeking any lists, contracts, MOUs, and data sharing records that outlines which businesses and properties your agency has access. Examples include: Lowes, HOAs, business improvement districts.

I would like to note that the locations of these cameras are made public on OpenStreetMap through DeFlock's mapping work (https://maps.deflock.org/?lat=31.3239&lng=-85.8504&zoom=12.73) This being said, your department personally disclosing their locations can not hurt the system any more than the aforementioned project already has. This negates the idea that department transparency for citizens on this matter is an "operational security threat"

Far more compromising to public safety than a records request, made to peer-review data collected by devices you allow subjecting citizens to, are the well-reported inaccuracies and abuse rates of these devices leading to wrongful detainment, arrest, officer misuse and credential breaches. 

Logins to Flock systems are available for purchase on the 'darknet'. Also, the cameras have been shown, contrary to Flock Safety statements, to store image captures and authorization keys on each device- even someone with a hacksaw could use the data for their own purposes, not just the blatantly corrupt federal agencies ALPR systems share data with.

Furthermore, with the Supreme Court ruling in Chatrie v United States (2026), these devices are unconstitutional. The federal government, superseding state legislation, ruled an expectation of privacy in location data which reveals your movements in the physical world, and even short-term surveillance of these movements is a search subject to the Fourth Amendment. 

Hiring a third-party should not allow courting Constitutional violations.

This information may also be found in Flock Safety or other ALPR company emails that alert the department that a business or private entity is sharing their cameras with you; no new records creation will be necessary- only use of existing records- though creation would be a valuable use of taxpayer money, given the mounting public interest in surveillance technology.

Please search 2023 to today’s date.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 10 business days.

Sincerely,

André Natta, a citizen of Alabama, in coordination with Jonathan Harris.

Pursuant to the Colorado Open Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

Thank you for the records your office released on October 7, 2026 in response to my earlier request (REQ-2026-942). I am writing with a separate, narrow request arising from them.

Under the Colorado Criminal Justice Records Act, C.R.S. §§ 24-72-301 et seq., I request access to and copies of the following:

The two telephone recordings described in the released briefing document "LCSO Impersonator Scam (as of 03/12/19)," prepared by Investigator Stephen Gates #08002. The document states that the Georgia Department of Corrections provided Investigator Gates with "2 phone recordings as evidence, during which he could hear what appeared to be scam calls being made in the background." The recordings were received in or about mid-2018 from GDC Special Agent Thomas Bisdorf and appear to be held as digital evidence in connection with your office's investigation of telephone impersonation fraud, including case 2017-9388. That case appears to be closed, based on these documents. 

Format. I request the recordings as electronic copies in their native format (or any common audio format). 

Redaction. I am not seeking the identities of any victims or private individuals. If a portion of either recording would disclose a crime victim's identity or other protected information, I ask that you redact that portion and release the remainder rather than withhold the recording entirely.

Why release is appropriate. I understand that release of criminal justice records other than records of official action is within your discretion, and that the Act defines criminal justice records to include recordings (C.R.S. § 24-72-302(4)). In exercising that discretion, I ask you to weigh the following:

- The recordings document a matter of substantial public interest: telephone fraud run from inside a Georgia state prison against Larimer County residents, which your office investigated beginning in 2017 and which your own records describe as affecting hundreds of local residents.

- The recordings contain no Larimer County victim's account. As described, they are recordings of activity inside a Georgia prison.
- Your office has already released the briefing document that describes them.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Illinois Freedom of Information Act., I hereby request the following records:

1. Policies and General Orders: All current department policies, general orders, standard operating procedures (SOPs), special orders, training manuals, or memoranda governing the Joliet Police Department's identification, documentation, tracking, and validation of individuals as suspected gang members, associates, or affiliates.
2. Criteria Guidelines: Any documents detailing the explicit threshold criteria used by JPD officers or specialized units (e.g., Gang Unit, Special Operations Group) to determine whether an individual is entered into a gang database or designated as gang-affiliated (including criteria regarding tattoos, clothing, associates, social media, or self-admission).
3. Database Specifications: Records detailing the name, architecture, vendor, and system parameters of any local database, software platform, or intelligence system utilized by JPD to store gang affiliation data.
4. communications.subject: Washington Public Records Act Request: (WA ESD 123) All Emails Sent to or Received from mcminimeelaw.com
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Washington Public Records Act, I hereby request the following records:

All electronic mail sent to or received from any email address operating under
the domain "mcminimeelaw.com" (matching the wildcard string *@mcminimeelaw.com)
exchanged with any district email account, alias, or internal
routing node, acting as either the author, sender, primary recipient,
carbon copy (CC), or blind carbon copy (BCC) holder.

The chronological scope of this request spans the entirety of the District's
available archival retention window.

TECHNICAL PRE-EXCLUSION OF REPETITIVE SYSTEM DATA:

To maximize administrative processing efficiency, accelerate delivery, and
eliminate unnecessary review burdens, the requester explicitly waives
interest in, pre-excludes, and requests the system-level filtering out of
the following non-substantive records categories:

1. Automated calendar invitations, change notifications, or updates.
2. Automated out-of-office or vacation autoreplies generated by either domain.
3. System-generated IT alerts, ticket confirmations, or password actions.

LIMITATION OF SCOPE & PRE-EXCLUSION OF SENSITIVE DATA:

The requester explicitly pre-excludes and waives any interest in the
Personally Identifiable Information (PII) of any individual student under FERPA.

Pursuant to RCW 42.56.210, if the District asserts that specific internal
staff names or student indicators are exempt from disclosure, the District is
required to apply narrow blackouts exclusively to those individual text strings
while releasing the remaining non-exempt text blocks, financial totals,
and generalized policy or administrative discussions.

Blanket withholding of entire records based on broad assertions of privilege
or exempt status is explicitly contested; only the minimal exempt portions
may be withheld.

MANDATORY STATUTORY COMPLIANCE TIMELINE:

As provided by RCW 42.56.520, a formal response is required within five (5)
business days.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Public Interest Mainstreaming Parenting
